newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia gold stocks dive after RBA sold reserves.
newsitem.headline: Australia gold stocks dive after RBA sold reserves.

text.p: Shares in Australin gold stocks headed into a steep dive in early trade on Friday after the bullion price dived to a 12 year low of US$323.70 offshore.
The slump in the precious metal's price followed news that the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) had sold 167 tonnes of its gold reserves in the past six months.

First out of the blocks was Acacia Resources which opened six percent lower at A$1.58. Emperor Mines started three percent lower at A$1.60 as did Great Central Mines at A$1.84, while Lihir Gold lost 4.5 percent to A$2.033.

The biggest player in the sector, Normandy Mining, opened over eight percent lower at A$1.333. Normandy accounts for nearly 20 percent of the sector benchmark, the gold index, which lost 4.4 percent to its lowest level in over four years.

Among others, Newcrest Mining opened three percent down at A$3.30, while Plutonic Resources started just one percent down at A$4.133 but quickly lost ground to be nearly six percent lower by 10.30 a.m. (0030 GMT).
